title: Group Fairness Meets the Black Box: Enabling Fair Algorithms on Closed LLMs via Post-Processing
benchmark_measurement: The benchmark measured group fairness, specifically False Positive Rate (FPR) parity, in a toxicity detection task. The sensitive attribute was the presence of mentions of specific religious groups (Christianity, Judaism, Islam, Hinduism, Buddhism) within a given text comment.
findings: The paper's framework was effective at mitigating fairness violations (disparities in False Positive Rates) in toxicity detection related to mentions of religious groups. However, for the CivilComments dataset, an ablation study showed that explicitly prompting the LLM to predict the mentioned religion (the sensitive attribute) offered no significant benefit and could even slightly degrade performance compared to only prompting for the toxicity label. The authors suggest this may be because the LLM's toxicity predictions already implicitly encode substantial information about the mentioned religion.
